This is just wrong. People should use [`int64_t`](https://en.cppreference.com/w/c/types/integer.html) (available since C99 / C++11) instead of `long int`, if a 64-bit wide integer is required. `long int` is not guaranteed to be 64 bits, but `int64_t` is. Neither is it guaranteed to have the same size as a pointer by the language standard.
